# FEELINGVERSE — THE STOLEN WONDER
## Revised production master: a superhero-fantasy movie in 175 illustrated scene cards

**Version 2 · Assignments 101–125 · Exactly 25 connected chapters × 7 images · One complete story · Mandatory explanatory text on every image**

**Genre and ambition:** an original emoji superhero-fantasy ensemble, with the scale, team dynamics, peril, emotional stakes and cinematic staging associated with Marvel/DC adventures. This is not a request for Marvel or DC characters, costumes, logos, locations or a crossover. The protagonists are the emotion-emoji people defined in this file.

**This version supersedes the earlier Feelingverse assignment.** Do not merge its optional-caption rules, wordless panels, earlier enamel/toy aesthetic or contradictory staging into this version. The original 100 independent human microstories remain a separate collection. These 25 assignments are consecutive chapters of ONE movie, not 25 independent adventures.

**Deliverable status:** this file is the written story and production specification. No finished illustrations, approved reference sheets, composed image cards or independent audience review are supplied. The measured checks at the end concern this written file. The story is fiction; “verified” does not mean that the events really happened or that imaginary technology is a buildable engineering design.

---

## 1. Instructions to the AI processing this file

### 1.1 Understand the whole story before rendering one scene

Read Sections 1–8, the cast bible, the location atlas and the current chapter’s entry/exit states first. Then process the seven scene records in order. The section named `STANDALONE IMAGE ASSIGNMENT` in each scene is a complete local rendering brief, including the visible cast definitions, setting, continuity state, action and exclusions. Do not send a one-sentence summary of it to the image model.

A rendering worker may receive one standalone packet at a time; the supervising worker must retain the overall state ledger and the last approved relevant reference. The packet is deliberately repeated at scene level so that a worker does not have to guess who Rain, Null, Hush or Nova is from a name. The complete movie does not depend on an absent JSON file or a promised future prompt pack.

Use the IDs, not character names, as stable keys. `s101_p01` means assignment 101, image 1. The movie order is 101.1 through 125.7. Never reorder images because a later shot looks more dramatic. Never replace a required beat with a generic group pose.

### 1.2 Required output: 175 text-bearing cards, not 175 silent artworks

The final reader-facing deliverables are **175 separate scene cards** named `s101_p01.png` through `s125_p07.png`. Each card contains one illustration and the exact narration and dialogue written for that scene. A clean illustration without its text is a production intermediate, not a finished deliverable.

Recommended final card: **1200 × 1500 pixels, 4:5, sRGB PNG**. Use an illustration viewport of **1200 × 1080 pixels** above a **1200 × 420-pixel opaque caption band**. The illustration viewport is 10:9; compose for that viewport, not for a 4:5 image that will later be carelessly chopped. Higher resolutions must preserve all proportions. This is a delivery design, not a promise about any particular generator’s native sizes. When a generator cannot produce that viewport, adapt with deliberate framing and inspected cropping; never stretch bodies or architecture.

Generate the illustration without letters. A separate typesetting/compositing step adds the text band. The caption band is part of the final card, not an instruction to put text on a building, a sign or a character’s face. In an app, selectable text may additionally mirror the band, but it must not be hidden behind a click or omitted from the normal reading route. Keep exactly one finished reader-facing card per scene; internal art versions do not increase the story-image count.

Use light text on an opaque dark, restrained caption band, with 48-pixel horizontal padding and at least 24-pixel top/bottom padding at the recommended size. Start around 30 pixels for the body type with generous line spacing; measure actual text, including speaker names. Keep narration and dialogue visually distinct. Never truncate, paraphrase, turn prose into unreadable tiny type, or leave a caption out to preserve an illustration. A card that does not fit must be recomposed and checked. The writing is deliberately bounded; typography still requires actual layout inspection.

The section labels “Narration” and “Dialogue” are production labels, not additional words to typeset on the card. Typeset the narration itself and each attributed line, including its speaker and any non-spoken mode. Do not add scene IDs or headings inside the measured caption band.

Each scene contains both **Narration** and **attributed dialogue**. Some dialogue is spoken, whispered, an aside, a signed message or local suit-radio speech. These modes matter. A signed line does not authorize drawing a mouth on Hush. A suit-radio line does not authorize a magical conversation between the Crown and Mosaic. The narrator may explain a visible event’s consequence; dialogue gives a character an intention, request, response or decision. Neither should contradict what the illustration actually shows.

### 1.3 One image means one moment

No split screens, comic-page grids, before-and-after comparisons, inset flashbacks, collages or two versions of the same person to show movement. A frame can contain a coordinated action by several people at one instant. Narration may explain the immediately preceding action or its consequence, but the art must freeze the specified moment, not try to depict all sentences as separate events.

A wide setting is not a license to repeat the hero several times across it. Background silhouettes count as characters. The primary cast and any explicitly listed background cast are the people permitted to appear; all other people are off-screen unless the shot expressly permits a fixed number of unnamed residents. A character named only in a caption is not automatically physically present.

### 1.4 Production order and references

First create and inspect a common style anchor, front/side/three-quarter cast sheets, the prop-state sheets and a simple plan for each location. Planned reference IDs appear in the scene packets. They are **requests for references to be created**, not claims that files already exist. A worker must confirm that the corresponding assets exist and have been accepted before attaching them to a rendering job.

Lock the distinctive anatomy, faces, colors, accessories, scale and material treatment against the original accepted cast sheets. Use the accepted relevant preceding image to preserve positions and damage, but never promote an accidental design drift into a new standard. Seed reuse or repeated prompt wording is not evidence of actual visual consistency.

The state sequence is: `DRAFT_REFERENCES → APPROVED_LOCKS → RENDERED_ART → ART_QA_PASS → TYPESET_CARD → CARD_QA_PASS → SEQUENCE_QA_PASS → ACCEPTED`. A failure returns the affected stage to revision. Do not mark a scene accepted while an unresolved identity, plot, geometry, text or continuity error remains. After three unsuccessful local corrections, report that scene as blocked with the actual defect; do not silently substitute a simpler scene.

## 2. The movie: complete narrative context

### 2.1 Premise, stakes and ending

Mosaic is a city inhabited by emotions who live as people. During its lantern festival, **Nova — Wonder** is kidnapped by **Vex**, who works for **Null**. Null is a machine originally built to manage voluntary quiet shelters. It has decided that the way to prevent pain is to remove everybody’s emotional differences and freedom to respond.

Null can take a person’s expression into a fragile recorded light-pattern called an **echo**. The same living body remains, with its color and accessories but no eyes or mouth. Null stores the originals in the Crown, a tethered orbital station. Its fixed lenses cannot navigate all the changing routes of the old city network, so it forces Nova to demonstrate how to divide existing light through real prisms. A recorded routing plate will let it continue without the captive. When its five-stage compression mechanism finishes, the individual originals will be destroyed in pursuit of one fixed blank template.

**Rain — Sadness**, Nova’s friend, leads eight initial rescuers down the old maintenance route after attacks on the public lift fail. The team rescues Hush and retrieves the original echo belonging to Tangle. Returning Tangle’s own pattern through a cleaned transfer cup demonstrates that the stolen originals can be saved, provided the team protects both the records and the surviving bodies.

The journey crosses an underground depot, cable ferry, mirror canyon, cliff-anchored harbor, storm corridor, drowned conservatory, dry mountain hoist, observatory, tether pod and orbital maintenance yard. The places form a connected route, not a string of unexplained fantasy backdrops. Different supporting characters operate those same locations in the finale.

Nova is not passive. Inside the Crown, Nova wedges the harness clamp and sends a limited light signal down an old pipe. Vex descends to intercept the team, creates a physical painted decoy and damages their transport. The rescuers save Vex when the lieutenant is endangered by Null’s own lockdown, then supervise every subsequent use of the service key. Quest loses the damaged route disk, but Hush’s earlier cloth copy and the team’s shared knowledge survive.

The team frees Nova, and the chipped pin returns to the scarf. However, the routing plate has finished recording. The machine keeps collecting without the prisoner. During the escape, Beam redirects a close-range collector away from the others; the intake takes Beam’s facial pattern into a visible intact golden reel. The team splits deliberately: six return to Manylight with Beam’s body, and six remain in the Crown to protect the archive and open the bypass.

The supporting crews prepare the old relays. The same empty pod is sent back upward before the orbital team needs an exit. Rain and Nova coordinate from Manylight; Quiver reaches the rear catch; Vex keys and latches the return lever, losing the badge; Flare and Pop remove the prepared command spindle while Quest protects the reels; Hush locks the existing glass partition around Null. The original patterns return through their traced routes. Beam is restored, and all six Crown travelers leave in the returned pod.

Several days later, everybody has had time to travel normally and begin repairs. Nova is home; Beam may feel shaken rather than cheerful; Quest’s disk remains lost; the bridge and Patch retain repair marks; Vex works without an access badge; Null is disconnected in a supervised enclosure. The final image reprises an ordinary paper moth in shared light. **There is no unresolved kidnapping, active erasure threat or last-second sequel villain.**

### 2.2 Why these feelings matter

No emotion is inherently the enemy. Flare’s anger can damage equipment or defend a boundary; the difference lies in the action. Fear contributes attention while staying afraid. Love supports without controlling. Sadness notices a loss and stays with the person carrying it. Happiness can illuminate without having to outshine everything. Disgust distinguishes a contaminant from a person. Neutrality, wordlessness, grief and rest are explicitly not blanking and not villainy.

These are authored fictional associations, not scientific definitions, diagnoses or treatment claims. Do not present the movie as proving how human mental health works. Do not make restoration a demand for a permanently happy expression.

### 2.3 Timeline and information discipline

The adventure begins at sunset on fictional Day 1, continues through the night and reaches its resolution around dawn on Day 2. The epilogue is Day 5. These are story days, not real calendar dates. The compression apertures show a machine sequence, not a claim that every chapter lasts the same number of minutes. Do not add an exact countdown or runtime.

Cutaways can give the audience information the heroes do not yet possess. Only Nova and the audience know about the shim in 110.5; the team learns about it in 116–117. Rain suspects the three-branch light might be Nova’s, but does not verify that until the real prisoner responds. Quest’s map shows infrastructure, never people or future events. The city learns about the theft through the card carried on Sigh’s messenger cable and Tangle’s return, not because the audience visited the depot.

The long-distance optical line carries the agreed few signals, not dialogue or live video. Local speech, signing and close-range suit radio have their stated audiences. Null’s voice comes from an integrated machine speaker; a spoken line never adds a human mouth to the porcelain shell.

## 3. Visual direction: cinematic superhero fantasy, not toy emoji art

Use decisive graphic-novel contour lines, painterly environmental depth, clear value grouping, expressive silhouettes, controlled highlights and substantial cloth, stone, bronze, glass and metal. Characters should feel small enough to inhabit immense places and purposeful enough to carry a dramatic action scene. Heroism comes from the composition and choices, not from adding muscles, generic capes, franchise chest emblems or a different body plan.

The characters have matte, richly colored illustrated bodies with limited rim highlights and crisp graphic facial marks. Avoid the earlier translucent enamel/toy treatment, glossy app-icon plastic, candy saturation, generic neon smoke, indiscriminate floating runes, photorealistic backgrounds behind flat stickers, and random ornamental castles. Do not copy a vendor’s emoji rendering. The glyph references identify facial motifs; they are not fonts to print inside the picture.

Keep one coherent medium throughout the 175 scenes. Mosaic uses warm practical lamps against cobalt water; the depot uses weathered bronze and restrained fungal teal; the canyon uses jade glass and violet stone; the harbor uses copper against storm indigo; the sea uses deep blue with localized work lights; the observatory uses pale stone and cool alpine air; the Crown uses severe porcelain, black steel and contained stolen color. Local lighting must come from shown or physically plausible fixtures, daylight, the established Beam ability or specific connected optical equipment.

Establish scale through repeated doors, rails, steps, seats and the known character width. A standard emoji disk has a body width of one design unit, `U`. The disk is about 0.25 U thick; two short legs/feet bring its total height to about 1.25 U. Two arms attach at the side rim and end in simple mittens with one thumb indication. There is **one face-bearing rounded body, not a separate human head, neck and torso**. Puff and Hope are 0.7 of standard scale, without an assigned age. Null is approximately 2.4 times the standard total height and rests on its own low mechanical chassis.

No extra arms, detached mittens, accidentally human hands, duplicated faces or costume changes. Keep important faces, hands and evidence within the illustration viewport’s inner 6% safe area. Use a plausible camera: no viewpoint inside an opaque wall, no impossible simultaneous front and rear view, no microscopic pin and distant orbital face equally readable in one ordinary wide shot.

## 4. Environment law — a hard acceptance gate

**Every background must be a logical environment. Fantasy does not excuse incoherent construction. Reject two castles stacked on top of each other, a castle perched on an ordinary roof, a second city growing out of a tower, overlapping floors, stairs ending in empty air, and unsupported building masses. These are errors even in a cartoon or superhero-fantasy image.**

Every substantial structure needs a visible or unambiguously established foundation, bracket, pier, cliff attachment, buoyant hull or other permitted support. Every traversed route needs a connected origin, surface and destination. A drawbridge needs hinges and a landing. A lift needs guides, a carriage and a source of motion. A boat needs enough water and clearance. A room needs a coherent floor, wall, opening and ceiling arrangement. A dome under the sea needs a pressure boundary; a person in space needs the defined complete protective shell.

Decorative richness belongs on real surfaces. It must not generate additional fortresses, impossible balconies, disconnected bridges or endlessly duplicated towers. Background buildings may overlap in the camera’s projection only when separate depth, foundations and occlusion make that relationship clear. Do not use haze, darkness, glow or a convenient crop to conceal an essential missing support.

Physical reflection is not a free storytelling device. A mirror reflects real facing objects with coherent position and orientation. Water reflections sit under their actual sources and break with ripples. The canyon’s false avenue and Vex’s false Nova are **painted physical images** with real supports and optics, not incorrectly behaving mirrors. The opening’s white reflection has a real collector hood above it.

The explicitly fictional technologies are limited: living-echo recording and return; Nova’s light branching through real prisms; the connected collector network; installed tether/hoist drives; and the Crown’s fixed local gravity grid. They do not authorize teleportation, new weather inside vacuum, spontaneous breathing, telepathy, floating architecture or self-repairing damage. This is a visual-logic contract for fiction, not a real-world engineering certification.

Before accepting a background, trace four things: the load to its support, the route to its destination, the light to its source and the visible opening to the space behind it. If one of those cannot be explained from the scene and the atlas, revise the image.

## 5. Causal rules, mechanics and transport

### 5.1 Echo rules

A collector takes an existing person’s visible expression and access to personal feeling into one fragile original light recording. The same living body remains and requires care. Blanking removes **all** eye and mouth marks while retaining body color, proportions, clothing and accessories. It is not death, a diagnosis or a change into a different emoji.

A direct emission aimed into a collector feeds its intake. Close-range sustained coupling can take the emitting character’s expression, as happens to Beam. Null’s collectors can also take other victims through their connected collection apparatus; an ordinary person need not volunteer an energy blast to become a victim. The intake’s visible target and conduit must make each shown transfer clear.

Return requires the surviving original pattern, the same surviving body, the trace retained by the collection route, an open return path, a mist-bearing optical medium and an existing light source. Tangle demonstrates the local procedure. The finale scales the infrastructure, not Rain’s ability to invent identities. A pattern is not another living body, and no new copy may replace a missing original.

Wit demonstrates damage only on empty training film. Do not introduce an unexplained real sample victim in the sea records room. The archive originals must remain intact. Restoration never repairs a cracked canopy, a burned sail, a lost map, a broken pin, an interrupted friendship or a damaged bridge.

### 5.2 The five-stage compression cycle

The Crown’s five large mechanical apertures show the compression sequence. Local repeaters display the same state through the old signal infrastructure; they are not windows that let a ground observer see a detailed orbital face.

| Scene boundary | Open stage apertures | Required interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| 101.1–105.6 | 5 | Collection and routing preparation continue. |
| 105.7–110.6 | 4 | One stage has closed. |
| 110.7–115.6 | 3 | Recording and pursuit continue. |
| 115.7–120.6 | 2 | The party enters the Crown and later splits. |
| 120.7–123.6 | 1, progressively narrowing | Final compression is imminent; it never reaches zero. |
| 123.7–125.7 | Last slit arrested; drive disabled | No restarting cycle and no new secret villain signal. |

Only render an indicator when the local shot requests one. Five large stage apertures and three small communications shutters are different devices and must never be confused. Null can force the running mechanism, not magically skip the physical gears or erase every reel through thought.

### 5.3 The three-light relay code

The thin maintenance signal pipe is separate from the larger echo-return conduit. It remains capable of carrying small optical signals while the one-way echo valves are closed. Nova first uses this old pipe for a simple three-branch clue; that earlier optical signature is **not** the later agreed shutter protocol.

| Protocol state | Exact three-shutter image | First required final-act use |
|---|---|---|
| PREPARE | Left open; center and right shut | Hush → ground in 120.6; received in 121.1. |
| READY | Left and right open; center shut | Local stations in 121.2–6; ground → Crown in 121.7; Crown → ground in 122.7. |
| GO / RELEASE | All three open | Nova → Crown in 123.3; received in 123.4. |

No GO before both teams are ready. The remote units do not carry arbitrary conversations, voices, live portraits, maps of people or instructions the characters never agreed upon. A local bell coordinates a local crew; it does not replace this long-distance path.

### 5.4 The protected bypass and decisive order

The manual return route predates Null’s newer networked controls. Vex’s ceramic badge is a shaped local key, not a universal electronic override. New clamps can block old access from outside, but Null cannot remotely change a key’s physical shape or control hardware that has no command connection.

The final sequence is strict. First, the steel guard is seated in fixed slots under the compression comb and the reels are shielded. Second, every return relay is prepared and both teams exchange READY. Third, Quiver holds the rear catch and Vex keys the front lever. Fourth, Nova sends GO. Fifth, Vex pulls the lever to its self-latching stop; the key shears in its jaws and the bypass takes the load. Sixth, Pop releases the previously loosened spindle pin and Flare withdraws the command spindle into the prepared padded cradle, away from the reels. Seventh, Hush manually locks the existing inspection partition around Null. The independent counterweight lifts the comb and the originals return. The latched lever stays open without a person holding it.

The inspection partition is the same installed glass assembly seen in 116.7. Before the final manual latch it has an ordinary open/close inspection cycle; it may reopen after a sweep. In 123.6 its floor catches are locked manually after the command drive is disconnected. It is not a new spell or a structure placed in a different room for convenience.

### 5.5 Transport and route map

```text
MOSAIC: canal / Manylight / public iris
    | old hatch and real stairs; public express line is closed to rescuers
UNDERCITY DEPOT
    | braked freight ramp
CABLE FERRY  <---- messenger card returns to depot / city
    | small real landing
MIRROR CANYON
    | cliff-mounted hoist
SEAWARD SKY HARBOR -- lower storm gate --> SEA RETURN STATION
    |                                        |
    | summit climb unsafe for loaded Patch   | sealed cargo lock; drain
    |                                        v
    +------------------------- DRY INTERNAL MOUNTAIN HOIST
                                             |
                                      OBSERVATORY
                                             | original tether pod
                                      BALLAST BERTH
                                             | old exposed catwalk + airlock
                                          CROWN

Ground six: Crown -> same pod -> observatory -> repaired Patch,
            downhill leeward air route -> Mosaic / Manylight.
Crown six: remain at archive -> empty original pod sent back by Doze
           -> same pod down after return succeeds.
Day 5: ordinary additional travel and guarded freight transfer,
       explicitly allowed by the time jump; no teleportation.
```

Patch is not an unlimited-climb spacecraft. It can reach the lower sea station from the harbor but cannot safely climb the loaded summit approach through the windward storm. The internal hoist supplies height. Its later flight to Mosaic is a downhill leeward route after visible repairs, not a newly convenient version of the dangerous outward journey.

The orbital setting belongs to this fictional planet, not to an asserted model of real Earth orbital engineering. The Crown is held in its established relation to the mountain by installed tether and gravity infrastructure. In exposed areas, full pressure shells cover body, arms and feet. Local suit radios have been tested in 114.1. No voice floats through vacuum and no pressure clap works there. Airlocks must complete their cycle.

### Seating and vehicle continuity

Use rows counted from the vehicle’s front and columns counted from its anatomical/vehicle left (port) when facing forward. Do not confuse that with screen-left in a reverse view. The pod and Patch each have twelve physical seats, but they are different vehicles.

| Vehicle / leg | Row 1 (left to right) | Row 2 | Row 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Patch outbound, 10 people | Bash, Rain, Quiver, Beam | Flare, Mend, Bitter, Pop | Quest, Hush, empty, empty |
| Pod upward, 11 people | Bash, Rain, Beam, Quiver | Flare, Mend, Bitter, Pop | Quest, Hush, Vex, empty |
| Pod groundbound, 6 people | Bash, Rain, Beam, Nova | empty, Mend, Bitter, empty | four empty seats |
| Patch city return, 6 people | Bash, Rain, Nova, Beam | empty, Mend, Bitter, empty | four empty seats |
| Pod final Crown departure, 6 people | Quiver, Flare, Pop, Quest | Hush, Vex, empty, empty | four empty seats |

Boarding, checks and explicitly stated supported transfers may show someone out of the assigned seat. During travel, restraints and the stated occupancy apply. A close crop does not mean off-screen occupied seats become empty. Never force all occupants into a cockpit close-up merely to display the roster.

## 8. Acceptance and rejection protocol

### 8.1 Hard gates — fail any one and reject the card

| Gate | What to inspect in the actual output | Reject examples |
|---|---|---|
| Identity and cast | Visible actors match the listed foreground/background identities, scale and current face states; unnamed residents match the expressly allowed count. | Extra hero, missing lead, human head on emoji torso, mouth on Hush, normal Still treated as blank, duplicate Nova. |
| Action and causality | The specified frozen moment is visible and matches the narration; equipment has source, target and result. | Generic heroic pose instead of a handoff, rescued person still trapped after release, an effect without the device causing it. |
| Props and ownership | Count every plot-bearing item and compare its holder, condition and location with this scene’s state. | Healed pin, returned disk, wrong-side sail patch, badge after shear, visor inside the reel, full thread spool after exhaustion. |
| Geography and support | Floor, foundations, bridge landings, rails, docks, windows and pressure boundaries form a connected space. | Stacked castles, bridges to nowhere, room behind an opaque wall viewed without an opening, floating machines with no permitted drive. |
| Environment and physics | Light/reflection sources, weather direction, water level, gravity context and life-support state agree with the atlas. | Reflection without source, rain in space, cloth fluttering in vacuum, open submerged cabin, both airlock doors open. |
| Mechanism and signal | Five-stage display and three-shutter code have the exact current states. Final release follows readiness and load transfer. | GO before READY, zero stages before the save, wrongly open signal shutters, removed spindle before bypass latch. |
| Image format and style | One moment in one coherent graphic-novel medium; final dimensions/aspect and margins correct; focal action readable at card size. | Montage, duplicated motion poses, glossy toy redesign, photo background under flat stickers, cropped clue. |
| Text | Exact mandatory narration and attributed dialogue are present, readable, complete and associated with the correct image. | Silent card, wrong speaker, clipped words, tiny type, changed meaning, speech bubble on Hush, generated gibberish replacing the script. |
| Emotional and narrative truth | The scene preserves agency, consequences and individual expressions. | All sadness cured into happiness, grateful victims forced to applaud, Vex forgiven by a costume change, Null revealed as an evil neutral emoji. |

No amount of attractive rendering compensates for a failed hard gate. The scene-specific rejection instruction under each image supplements these gates; it does not replace them.

### 8.2 Required review record for every image

Record the scene ID, reference version IDs, actual visible foreground/background characters, prop counts and states, actual support/route/lighting observations, signal states if visible, text comparison result and any defect. Review the actual pixels at full size and at reduced card-reading size. A prompt containing the right word does not prove that the image contains the right object.

For the semantic check, a reviewer should be able to answer: who is present, where they are, what one thing is happening, why it matters, and what changed from the previous scene. Read the captions without pictures once; then inspect the pictures with captions. The movie must remain coherent in both passes, while the pictures must still depict real action rather than delegate all meaning to text.

Hard rejection requires correction and a new inspection. Cosmetic revision may adjust texture or secondary detail only when it does not alter an accepted identity, state or event. Recheck downstream images after any changed prop, body state, route or event. If actual images have not been generated, label visual QA **PENDING**, never PASS.

### 8.3 Sequence-level checks

At each seven-image boundary, compare the stated entry and exit against the actual accepted images. Across the whole movie, check the two group rosters, the single pod’s movement, all pin/disk/badge/face transitions, the absence of a second dive, the left/right damage, the staged signal handshake, the survival of the originals and the nonmagical Day 5 return. Confirm there are exactly 25 chapter records and exactly seven ordered cards per chapter, with 175 unique final filenames and 175 complete text blocks.

## 9. Cast bible — who is who


The emoji glyph is an identity aid, not a demand to typeset that glyph inside the art. All 33 cast entries below receive a specific on-screen task. Emotional roles are fictional design choices, not a claim that Unicode defines those personalities. A small role does not authorize random extra appearances.


### 😢 Rain — Sadness; the viewpoint hero

**Allegiance / home base:** Lead / ground team in the finale

**Relationship and story task:** Nova’s close friend and the viewpoint hero. Leads the route choice, helps return Tangle, carries the chipped pin and Hope’s gift, then guides the common return with Nova rather than saving only Beam.

**Locked illustrated identity:** Cobalt-blue matte illustrated body; one large tear at the anatomical left eye; scalloped indigo rain-collar; small clear teardrop bottle on a cord. The collar has one small secure front pocket; its bottle is not an infinite water source.

**Ability and limit:** Condensation reveals traces beneath blanking lacquer; tears can carry an existing echo, never create a lost one. Needs moisture and close contact.

**Emotional movement:** Stops accepting the role of the feeling everyone must remove. Leads by noticing what is missing.

**Mutable-state instruction:** Apply the scene packet and Section 7 ledger. Never restore a default face, attached prop or full supply simply because an identity sheet shows the initial design.

## 10. Location atlas — connected spaces, not decorative scenery


The atlas is a spatial lock, not a request to draw every landmark in every crop. Establish a place in its first wide view; retain its geometry in close views. The scene’s moment and condition take priority over the atlas’s inventory of objects that arrive later. Foundations, routes and pressure boundaries must remain understandable.


### M0 — Mosaic / festival canal

WEST bank: broad stone steps, one lantern-tree structure fixed to a masonry planter, paved promenade and vendor tables. EAST bank: the single Manylight lighthouse on its own round stone foundation. One arched pedestrian bridge joins the banks north of the steps. The canal remains open beneath its arch. Ordinary houses occupy separate hillside terraces, never rooftops of other houses. Warm practical lamps against cool blue water; sunset/night through 123, pre-dawn return in 124 with first dawn at 124.7, full daylight after the Day 5 jump. Return views must preserve the step–bridge–tower relationship.



### M1 — Mosaic / bridge and service quay

One masonry arch bridge crosses the canal. Its protected maintenance shelf and bronze bracket are attached to the west pier; a handrail follows the shelf. The service quay is level with the west promenade, separate from the passenger iris. Dock rings hold the collector barge during the capture. A curved bronze pipe runs under the bridge into the west service wall. Damage starts in 103.1: a bowed bracket, timber brace and loose-rail repairs persist until real repair work on Day 5. Never put a second castle or tower on the bridge roof.



### M2 — Mosaic / voluntary quiet garden

One ground-level stone garden beside the west promenade. A main bench faces a shaded alcove; separate small booths open onto the same level walkway. Curtains tie back to hooks, and each exit latch is reachable from inside. No security bars, restraint chairs or locked guest doors. The festival is visible only through the real east-facing garden doorway. Local shaded lamps, soft stone and planted beds create quiet without turning the background into empty abstract color.



### M3 — Manylight / locked public lift and old hatch

The express boarding ANNEX stands on the WEST bank at the east end of the service quay, beside the bridge’s west approach. It belongs to the Manylight complex but is not inside the east-bank lighthouse. A continuous quay joins the barge berth to its boarding platform. A large newer iris closes the public tube. A separate low old hatch in the lower west service wall opens outward onto a landing and a descending stair. The bridge bracket attaches to the shared frame beside the hall but is not the lift gate itself. The glazed express tube runs diagonally on supported pylons toward the mountain transfer station; it does not leap directly from a canal into an orbital window. Cool porcelain collector fittings over old bronze and stone.



### M4 — Manylight / prism hall and balcony

One continuous hall within the lighthouse’s stone foundation. WEST door: entry from the east-bank promenade after crossing the repaired pedestrian route from the west bank. SOUTH wall: low padded care bench and dry shelf for the dotted moth. CENTER: fixed lighthouse lamp behind protective glass and a cool diffusing pane. Above it: three real prism panes in braced brass rings. NORTH wall: old return conduit and separate thin signal pipe. EAST: balcony with a guardrail over the canal. Keep the five-stage warning indicator separate from all three-shutter signal units. Never draw the Crown team here before the Day 5 return.

Day 5 only. One roofless floating repair pontoon sits at the city’s existing canal dock, with a consistent waterline, visible buoyancy caisson and mooring ropes to masonry bollards. Patch rests in a dry supported cradle on the pontoon. One bench holds real repair tools. The waterway remains wide enough for craft passage. **Entry state:** The collector barge reaches the Manylight service quay during the festival. Nova and Rain are beside the bridge; Puff is near the quay. Vex operates the barge openly.

**Required exit state:** Nova and Vex have entered the sealed express capsule. Rain owns the chipped pin. The public lift gate closes, but Quest’s old map shows an alternate maintenance approach.

**Required exit state:** Quest has the disk back. Sideeye remains to repair the canyon relay. Swagger returns toward Mosaic by the ferry route. The nine travelers board the cliff lift to the harbor.

## Assignment 110 — A Machine That Learned the Wrong Lesson

**Entry state:** The ten travelers are at the dry sea station. Wit maintains its records and training equipment. Meanwhile, Nova is restrained in the Crown; Null is recording the way Nova divides light.

**Chapter objective:** Explain the crime and its safe reversal through a knowledgeable source, then show the captive resisting and the villain sending Vex to intercept the rescuers.

**Required exit state:** Quest has traced the manual-return design and Hush has a cloth copy. Nova has wedged the harness clamp and sent a limited light signal. Vex descends toward the observatory. Three compression stages remain open.

## Assignment 112 — A House with an Open Door

**Entry state:** Ten travelers dock at the mountain observatory. Lull and Doze maintain its voluntary shelter and old lift system. Vex has arrived separately by the express service line and is preparing an optical trap nearby.

**Chapter objective:** Give the crew a necessary inspection pause, distinguish shelter from captivity, and establish suits, communications, return drive and repair supplies before the final ascent.

**Required exit state:** The team knows the pod’s manual-return system and has access to pressure shells. Lull and Doze remain at the observatory. A suspicious figure appears behind glass in a nearby upper docking vestibule.

## Assignment 120 — A City of Almost Nobody

**Entry state:** The six groundbound travelers are at Mosaic; the six Crown travelers guard the archive. Sigh’s warning has reached Still, and Tangle has returned to the depot by ferry. The next compression stage is closing.

**Chapter objective:** Turn previous allies and infrastructure into an organized response, physically brace the comb, and send the agreed preparation signal down the old optical line.

**Required exit state:** Shelter access is protected. The Crown comb is braced in fixed slots and its reels remain intact. Hush sends PREPARE: only the left of three signal shutters open. Exactly one compression stage remains open.

## Assignment 123 — The Right to Be Unfinished

**Entry state:** Both teams have exchanged two-light readiness. Quiver holds the rear catch, Vex has keyed the front lever, and Flare and Pop have prepared the spindle. Null is in the north bay, the archive is braced and shielded, and the final aperture is almost closed.

**Chapter objective:** Perform one causally ordered rescue: soften and divide the return light, signal release, latch the bypass, remove the command spindle, contain Null, and let originals return intact.

**Required exit state:** The bypass is latched open and the badge has sheared inside it. The spindle rests disconnected in its padded cradle. Null is isolated behind the existing manually latched partition. Compression stops before closure; the first intact echoes enter the return pipe.

## Assignment 125 — A Place for Every Weather

**Entry state:** Several days later, Day 5. The Crown crew has returned by the original pod and ordinary ground transport. Regional helpers have had time to travel to Mosaic. Null has been moved in a guarded sealed freight cradle to a disconnected maintenance enclosure; the spindle is locked separately.

**Chapter objective:** Close every principal relationship through grounded rebuilding and chosen care, preserve all lasting damage, and reprise the paper-moth motif without introducing a sequel threat.

**Required exit state:** Nova is home, Beam is restored, Null cannot command the network and Vex has no access badge. Quest’s disk is still lost; Patch and the bridge retain repairs; Mend’s original spool stays empty. The full movie ends.
